title: kv-cache: improved eviction/defrag heuristics and spillover backpressure
author: Diego Marquez
description: Motivation: KV cache fragmentation and uncontrolled spillover can cause large latency spikes and memory churn on high-concurrency workloads. This PR implements heuristic updates to eviction and defragmentation scheduling and introduces backpressure for spillover/paging paths to avoid cascading OOMs. Scope: changes are limited to the serving runtime KV cache layer and its scheduler; no public API changes. Design summary: 1) introduce a fragmentation score per shard computed from contiguous live entry density; 2) trigger opportunistic defragmentation when score exceeds threshold and GPU memory headroom is low; 3) implement spillover backpressure token bucket that slows admission of new KV write-heavy requests when paging I/O latency exceeds a threshold; 4) prioritize eviction of large, low-reuse entries using a combined cost metric (size * recency_decay); 5) add metrics and tracing for fragmentation, defrag runs, spillover queue length and backpressure events. Checklist: - [x] Design doc link: https://linear.app/redwood/board/ENG-8721 - [x] Unit tests for metric computation and token bucket - [x] Benchmarks (perf-canary) showing reduced tail latency under synthetic fragmentation - [x] E2E smoke test against dedicated docker image - [x] Observability dashboard + alerting thresholds Notes: defaults are conservative; feature gated behind runtime flag kv.defrag_enabled and kv.spillover_backpressure_enabled to allow staged rollout.
commits: Initial defrag scoring and eviction metric implementation
Add spillover token-bucket and admission control
Integrate defrag scheduler with memory headroom signal
